topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Spans to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisites & Linear Combinations
lecture_lines: Vectors are arrows from origin to points.
Combine vectors by scaling and adding.
This creates new vectors in space.
animations: Display two vectors v1 and v2 on a #FFFFFF canvas.
Animate scalar multiplication: c1*v1 and c2*v2.
Show their sum: c1*v1 + c2*v2.
Color change to highlight the resulting vector.
Scale the vectors to show the linear combination result.

sections.title: The Concept of Span
lecture_lines: Span is the reach of vectors.
One vector spans a simple line.
Two vectors span a flat plane.
animations: Start with a single vector v in #FFFF00.
Show the line formed by all scalar multiples of v.
Add a second vector w not on the line.
Display the full 2D plane as their span.
Highlight the filled plane with a light #8888FF shade.

sections.title: Linear Dependence vs. Independence
animations: Start with two vectors pointing in the same direction.
Show one vector as a scaled version of other.
Label them linearly dependent in red #FF0000.
Introduce a third vector not in their span.
Label the set linearly independent in green #00FF00.

sections.title: Bases: The Minimum Building Blocks
animations: Show a 2D grid of unit vectors.
Demonstrate that any vector can be formed by them.
Remove one vector and show the gap.
Add a new vector and show the coverage restored.
Label this set as a basis in bold #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Summary & Application
animations: Summarize span and independence as core concepts.
Show a practical example using coordinates #AAAAAA.
Display final conclusion text on #000000 background.
